details.report:
Implemented bounded opaque Reviewer runner in src/reviewer-agent.ts and migrated its owning tests. Runner consumes AcceptedReviewerDispatch only, validates cardinality/axes and prompt byte evidence before setup, verifies accepted target/ref/object identity, creates one mirror plus isolated concurrent leg workspaces, preserves active provider/model/auth, exposes each exact accepted tool subset, exact-matches bash command strings, returns axis-keyed report/usage/target/prompt bytes-length-SHA/workspace evidence, and retains failed/cancelled workspaces.

TDD evidence: RED was captured before implementation (`RED: opaque accepted-dispatch run seam missing`). GREEN: `npm run typecheck` passes; focused `node --import tsx --test test/reviewer-agent.test.ts` passes 4/4. Same-pattern dispatch tests also passed 10/10 in the combined focused run. Behavior facts covered include one/two leg cardinality, overlapping two-leg execution, exact prompt identity, pinned shallow refs, exact one-tool visibility, byte-exact bash denial without widening, auth/provider delegation, workspace isolation/deletion, and cancellation retention.

Introduced-regression check: full `npm test` ran 359 tests: 357 passed, 2 failed solely at the intentionally unmigrated old Reviewer lifecycle seam: `every mandated Reviewer fatal stage aborts print and JSON at its intended seam` and `installed npm tarball runs native Reviewer expansion in an independent consumer repository`. Exact residual next slice: migrate reviewer-role.ts, role-runtime/extension wiring, reviewer-execution-ledger types/evidence, reviewer auditor input, package-lifecycle integration, and old fatal-stage expectations to dispatch-owner -> opaque-runner results; then remove the clearly internal deprecated `runReviewerAgent` adapter, which currently fails closed rather than creating a second lifecycle owner. No Soul changes were needed; audit found no runner-specific principle appropriate for Soul.
